lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to make a sprite jump by setting its velocity upward, only when it is standing on the floor.
To jump, set vy to a positive number like 14.
Gravity takes over: the sprite rises, slows down, stops at the top, then falls.
Without a check, players can jump in mid-air forever.
Only jump if the sprite is on the floor.
Because gravity changes vy a little each frame, a jump makes a smooth curve — like a ball thrown in the air.
Stronger gravity makes jumps shorter and snappier.
Tuning these numbers is real game design.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
